XD-ADR-0001.content: The system model is written in **SysML v2 textual notation** (``.sysml``).
XD-ADR-0001.title: SysML v2 textual notation for the system model

XD-ADR-0002.content: Views are rendered as **drawio** files by our own tooling. Content comes from the model; manual **layout tweaks are kept** when views are regenerated. Revised by :need:`XD-ADR-0037`: layout keeping moves to iteration 2.
XD-ADR-0002.title: Views as drawio files rendered from the model

XD-ADR-0003.content: **Agents are first-class**: they edit and review design content the same way human engineers do.
XD-ADR-0003.title: Agents are first-class

XD-ADR-0004.content: **Trace rule:** trace annotations go right-to-left in the V-model and from concrete to abstract. The more concrete artifact holds the link; backlinks are only ever computed. Refined by :need:`XD-ADR-0030`.
XD-ADR-0004.title: Trace rule: the concrete side holds the link

XD-ADR-0005.content: Requirements (stakeholder needs, system requirements) are written in **sphinx-needs**. SysML elements reference them by ID (see :need:`XD-ADR-0036`).
XD-ADR-0005.title: Requirements in sphinx-needs

XD-ADR-0006.content: Repos are managed as a multi-repo workspace with **west**.
XD-ADR-0006.title: A multi-repo workspace with west

XD-ADR-0007.content: The main SYSMOD reference is https://mbse4u.com/sysmod/.
XD-ADR-0007.title: SYSMOD is the main method reference

XD-ADR-0008.content: **Prototypes are first-class.** Prototype setups (e.g. Nucleo + breakouts) are part of the model and are traced like the product design. Refined by :need:`XD-ADR-0031`.
XD-ADR-0008.title: Prototypes are first-class

XD-ADR-0009.content: Requirements use **EARS** sentence patterns. Refined by :need:`XD-ADR-0039`.
XD-ADR-0009.title: Requirements use EARS

XD-ADR-0010.content: The framework itself gets its **own Sphinx documentation**, separate from the example's design docs.
XD-ADR-0010.title: The framework has its own Sphinx documentation

XD-ADR-0011.content: The west manifest lives in a **dedicated manifest repo**.
XD-ADR-0011.title: A dedicated manifest repo

XD-ADR-0012.content: All repos are hosted on **GitHub**. CI runs on GitHub Actions; changes are reviewed through pull requests.
XD-ADR-0012.title: GitHub, GitHub Actions and pull requests

XD-ADR-0013.content: We design a **new ID prefix scheme**. The SEG IDs are not reused.
XD-ADR-0013.title: A new ID prefix scheme

XD-ADR-0014.content: We use the tool versions **installed on this machine**. A Docker image with all tools comes later.
XD-ADR-0014.title: Tool versions of the reference machine

XD-ADR-0016.content: The result is a **set of linked Sphinx documents** that describes the project in full: system architecture; SW requirements, SW architecture and design, SW test specification; ME and EE requirements; ME assembly design; one design doc per PCBA.
XD-ADR-0016.title: A set of linked Sphinx documents

XD-ADR-0017.content: Documents **extract content from the design models** where possible (SysML, FreeCAD, KiCad), the way API docs come from Doxygen comments.
XD-ADR-0017.title: Documents extract content from the models

XD-ADR-0018.content: Creating and storing **CAM data from CAD data** (ME and EE) is a task of the framework. Moved to iteration 2 by :need:`XD-ADR-0037`.
XD-ADR-0018.title: CAM data from CAD data is a framework task

XD-ADR-0019.content: All design outputs, including the pre-built firmware, go into a **bundle**. The user will share a bundling tool later. Terms fixed by :need:`XD-ADR-0034`; moved to iteration 2 by :need:`XD-ADR-0037`.
XD-ADR-0019.title: All design outputs go into a bundle

XD-ADR-0021.content: Each repo has **its own zdocs registry**. The manifest repo has a registry that builds the **full linked set**. Revised by :need:`XD-ADR-0029`: upstream docs are built locally, not used as remote documents.
XD-ADR-0021.title: One zdocs registry per repo, the full set in the manifest repo

XD-ADR-0022.content: Added documents: stakeholder needs and system requirements spec; system and integration test spec; EE and ME test specs; one doc per prototype setup.
XD-ADR-0022.title: More documents: needs, test specs, prototype setups

XD-ADR-0023.content: Trace IDs for CAD elements live **inside the CAD files** (KiCad symbol/sheet fields, FreeCAD object properties). Doc extraction reads them. Changed by :need:`XD-ADR-0128`: the IDs of boards, assemblies, ports and harnesses are owned by the domain model, and CAD files carry them only as references.
XD-ADR-0023.title: Trace IDs live inside the CAD files

XD-ADR-0024.content: ME CAM output is **3MF (and STL) plus a print-settings profile**. No G-code.
XD-ADR-0024.title: ME CAM output is 3MF and STL plus print settings

XD-ADR-0025.content: Generated outputs are **built by CI**: workflow artifacts on pull requests, release assets on tags. Revised by :need:`XD-ADR-0032`: drawio files are committed.
XD-ADR-0025.title: Generated outputs are built by CI

XD-ADR-0026.content: A bundle is one tag of the manifest repo. Superseded by :need:`XD-ADR-0034`.
XD-ADR-0026.title: A bundle is one tag of the manifest repo

XD-ADR-0027.content: **No document control** (``doc_control``) in iteration 1. Git history and PR reviews are enough for now.
XD-ADR-0027.title: No document control in iteration 1

XD-ADR-0028.content: Features that zdocs lacks are built as **separate Sphinx extensions in the framework repo**. Useful ones may move into zdocs later.
XD-ADR-0028.title: Missing zdocs features become Sphinx extensions in xdmod

XD-ADR-0029.content: **Cross-repo traces:** each repo's zdocs registry also **builds its upstream documents locally** from the west checkout that the manifest pins. This is how a downstream repo checks its links into upstream needs. (zdocs imports needs only from locally built documents.)
XD-ADR-0029.title: Upstream documents are built locally

XD-ADR-0030.content: **Link-type table:** :need:`XD-ADR-0004` stays the default. A table of link types names the owner side of each. Peer interfaces (e.g. EE↔SW pin map, EE↔ME connector positions) are **interface elements in syseng**, and both domains link to them. Allocation is stored on the concrete side. Changed by :need:`XD-ADR-0131` (SW reads the board pin maps from EE) and :need:`XD-ADR-0134` (ME writes board geometry into KiCad in a co-design change).
XD-ADR-0030.title: Link-type table and interface elements

XD-ADR-0031.content: **Prototype and product are variants** of one logical architecture (SysML v2 variants). A prototype test verifies the logical and SW requirements it covers. Product-specific requirements need product evidence. The vertical bar of iteration 1 is the **prototype variant**. Revised by :need:`XD-ADR-0092` to :need:`XD-ADR-0097`.
XD-ADR-0031.title: Prototype and product are variants

XD-ADR-0032.content: **Drawio files are committed**, and CI checks that they match the model. **HIL test results** are packaged with the user's bundling tool, the same way as design outputs.
XD-ADR-0032.title: drawio files are committed and checked

XD-ADR-0033.content: **The manifest is the only place that pins revisions.** A downstream PR's CI builds against the upstream revisions on the manifest's main branch. A change across several repos = one PR per repo + one manifest PR that bumps them together.
XD-ADR-0033.title: The manifest is the only place that pins revisions

XD-ADR-0034.content: **Terms:** a baseline is a tag of the manifest repo (a fixed set of repo versions). A bundle is the package of outputs (docs, CAM, firmware, HIL results) built from one baseline.
XD-ADR-0034.title: Terms: baseline and bundle

XD-ADR-0035.content: **FreeCAD storage and diff** (``.FCStd`` is a zip file) is decided in Phase 3, after hands-on research.
XD-ADR-0035.title: FreeCAD storage is decided after research

XD-ADR-0036.content: **SysML references to requirements:** a tool generates a package of **read-only requirement stubs** (ID + short name) from ``needs.json``. Nobody edits them by hand; CI checks that they match.
XD-ADR-0036.title: Read-only requirement stubs in SysML

XD-ADR-0037.content: **Moved to iteration 2:** CAM pipeline and bundle, the PDF document set, layout keeping in drawio, product PCB layout. Iteration 1 builds HTML docs only. Changed by :need:`XD-ADR-0142`, :need:`XD-ADR-0143` (CAM in iteration 1) and :need:`XD-ADR-0144` (a PCB layout without routing).
XD-ADR-0037.title: Scope moved to iteration 2

XD-ADR-0038.content: **Suspect/stale link detection:** study the user's tool **affirmatrix** (https://github.com/tiacsys/affirmatrix) in Phase 1.
XD-ADR-0038.title: Study affirmatrix for suspect links

XD-ADR-0039.content: EARS is used for **system and domain requirements**. Stakeholder needs may be plain statements.
XD-ADR-0039.title: EARS for system and domain requirements

XD-ADR-0040.content: **Every check also runs locally** (one command per repo), not only in GitHub Actions.
XD-ADR-0040.title: Every check also runs locally

XD-ADR-0041.content: In iteration 1, **GitHub CI only builds docs and runs trace checks**. Checks that need KiCad, FreeCAD or the Zephyr SDK run locally until the Docker image exists.
XD-ADR-0041.title: GitHub CI builds docs and runs trace checks only

XD-ADR-0042.content: **Repo names:** the framework (methods and tools) is **XDMOD** ("Cross-Domain MODeling", named like SYSMOD), repo ``xdmod``. Each tool in it gets a **Latin stem with a ``-trix`` suffix**, like affirmatrix and probatrix. The example repos use the prefix ``robarm-`` (``robarm-manifest``, ``robarm-syseng``, ``robarm-ee``, ``robarm-me``, ``robarm-sw``). Extended by :need:`XD-ADR-0066`: ``robarm-integration``.
XD-ADR-0042.title: Names: XDMOD, -trix tools, robarm- repos

XD-ADR-0043.content: **Merging:** trunk-based on ``main``. Every change goes through a PR, required checks must pass, and PRs are **rebase-merged** (linear history). Enforced with org rulesets.
XD-ADR-0043.title: Trunk-based merging with rebase

XD-ADR-0044.content: **Agent identity:** agents work under the user's account, and their commits carry a ``Co-Authored-By`` trailer. GitHub does not let you approve your own PR, so rulesets **require passing checks but no approval count**. The user's review and merge is the approval.
XD-ADR-0044.title: Agents work under the user's account

XD-ADR-0045.content: **Changes across repos:** the same branch name is used in every repo the change touches. CI checks out sibling repos at that branch if it exists, otherwise at the manifest pin. Upstream merges first, then one manifest PR bumps all pins.
XD-ADR-0045.title: One branch name across repos

XD-ADR-0046.content: **Planning:** ``plan.md`` stays the master plan. Tasks become GitHub issues in the repo where the work happens, and PRs close them. An org Projects board is optional.
XD-ADR-0046.title: Planning with plan.md, issues and PRs

XD-ADR-0047.content: **Tags:** each repo uses SemVer tags ``vX.Y.Z``. Baselines are manifest tags ``baseline/vX.Y.Z``, and their GitHub release carries the outputs.
XD-ADR-0047.title: SemVer tags and baseline tags

XD-ADR-0048.content: **Docs hosting:** GitHub Pages on the manifest repo hosts the full linked set, with ``main`` as "latest" plus one folder per baseline. PR docs are CI artifacts. This adds **multi-version hosting**, which zdocs lacks today. The model to follow is the tiacsys/bridle docs.
XD-ADR-0048.title: Docs hosting on GitHub Pages with versions

XD-ADR-0049.content: **X1 CI scope:** in iteration 1, GitHub CI builds docs and traces **without CAD content**, so its trace graph is partial. Full builds that include KiCad and FreeCAD content run only through the local one-command check (:need:`XD-ADR-0040`). Refines :need:`XD-ADR-0041`.
XD-ADR-0049.title: CI runs without CAD content

XD-ADR-0050.content: **X2 HIL evidence:** HIL run records (``sha256(zephyr.bin)``, manifest repo SHAs, Twister JUnit/JSON, evidence rule: clean tree and pinned versions) live on **their own orphan branch in robarm-sw**, the same idea as affirmatrix's ``case`` branch. The test report reads them from there. Revised by :need:`XD-ADR-0066`: the evidence branch lives in robarm-integration.
XD-ADR-0050.title: HIL evidence on an orphan branch

XD-ADR-0051.content: **X3 Agents and evidence:** agents analyse suspect links and prepare affirmations and verdicts, but **only a human's commit counts** as an affirmation or verdict. Refines :need:`XD-ADR-0003`.
XD-ADR-0051.title: Only a human's commit affirms

XD-ADR-0052.content: **X4 Suspect links:** we use **affirmatrix** and adapt it through **issues and PRs on tiacsys/affirmatrix**. Needed changes: read imported/upstream needs, accept open link types from our table (:need:`XD-ADR-0030`), take input from our needs.json extractors.
XD-ADR-0052.title: affirmatrix is adapted through upstream issues and PRs

XD-ADR-0053.content: **X5 SHAs:** rebase merge stays. **Evidence is recorded only against commits on ``main`` or baseline tags**, after merge. Runs on PR branches are previews and are not kept as evidence.
XD-ADR-0053.title: Evidence only from main or baseline commits

XD-ADR-0054.content: **X6 Cross-repo flow:** :need:`XD-ADR-0045` stays for PR CI. In addition, a **bump bot**: each merge to ``main`` in a robarm repo opens or updates a manifest bump PR, and that PR's CI builds the full set.
XD-ADR-0054.title: A bump bot for manifest pins

XD-ADR-0055.content: **X7 zdocs gaps** (version_project ignored for Sphinx docs; every indirect upstream doc must be listed by hand; no import-only mode) are fixed through **issues and PRs on tiacsys/zdocs**. Until those merge, the framework uses workarounds. Refines :need:`XD-ADR-0028` for these three gaps.
XD-ADR-0055.title: zdocs gaps are fixed upstream

XD-ADR-0056.content: **X8 FreeCAD storage** (resolves :need:`XD-ADR-0035`): ``.FCStd`` saved **uncompressed**, a git **textconv** for readable diffs, and a **review report** (drawing SVG, image diff, changed parameters and trace IDs) built locally and attached to the PR.
XD-ADR-0056.title: FreeCAD files uncompressed, with textconv and a review report

XD-ADR-0057.content: **Small corrections from research:** (a) a drawio file "matches the model" means its content (labels, parents, edge ends, kinds, links), not its geometry (:need:`XD-ADR-0032`); (b) stubs: ``concern`` for stakeholder needs, ``requirement`` for system requirements, so SYSMOD's ``frame`` link is kept (:need:`XD-ADR-0036`); (c) every doc build runs strict (``-W --keep-going``) with zdocs' CI pins (:need:`XD-ADR-0040`); (d) OCI tags map ``baseline/vX.Y.Z`` → ``X.Y.Z`` (:need:`XD-ADR-0047`); (e) a removed requirement is first marked ``retired``, and IDs are never reused; (f) devicetree trace IDs go in our own binding, never on upstream nodes; (g) CI checkouts use ``fetch-depth: 0`` and annotated tags; (h) link types are declared **per need type**, never globally (:need:`XD-ADR-0030`).
XD-ADR-0057.title: Small corrections from research

XD-ADR-0058.content: **SysML toolchain:** OMG Pilot Implementation through ``jshell`` for checking and JSON export; our own Python tools read that JSON; Sysand for libraries; SYSMOD library ``mbse4u/sysmod-sysmlv2``. Syside isn't used, because its CLI and Python library need a paid licence.
XD-ADR-0058.title: SysML toolchain: the OMG Pilot Implementation

XD-ADR-0059.content: **xdmod is in every workspace** that uses the framework, as a west project in its manifest.
XD-ADR-0059.title: xdmod is in every workspace

XD-ADR-0060.content: **All commands run from the workspace root** (the west topdir). That includes CLI tools (west, claude, doc builds, checks, extractors) and **launchers for GUI tools** (KiCad, FreeCAD and others), so paths and environment are set up correctly. git is the only exception.
XD-ADR-0060.title: All commands run from the workspace root

XD-ADR-0061.content: **One west topdir at the workspace root.** The root holds ``.west/``, ``.venv/``, ``build/`` and all repos.
XD-ADR-0061.title: One west topdir at the workspace root

XD-ADR-0062.content: **Agent material in repos:** each repo has a ``claude/`` subfolder. A **launch ``CLAUDE.md``** for the workspace root lives in xdmod and is **copied there during workspace bootstrap**.
XD-ADR-0062.title: Agent material in each repo's claude/ folder

XD-ADR-0063.content: This workspace's planning folder (``claude/``: plan, research, notes, mission brief) **moves to ``xdmod/claude/``** once the xdmod repo exists (Phase 4).
XD-ADR-0063.title: The planning folder moves into xdmod

XD-ADR-0064.content: **Every tool runs with a memory limit and a timeout**, for humans' scripts and all agents alike. The limits are set per tool and use. Swap is off inside the limit, so a runaway tool is killed and can't stall the machine or block agents. Interim wrapper: ``.venv/bin/xd-limit`` (systemd user scope + ``timeout``); xdmod's command layer takes this over (3.13).
XD-ADR-0064.title: A memory limit and a timeout for every tool

XD-ADR-0065.content: **Provenance on GitHub:** everything an agent posts on the user's behalf (issues, comments, PR descriptions, reviews, release notes) ends with the trailer ``🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)``. Commits keep the ``Co-Authored-By`` trailer. Extends :need:`XD-ADR-0044`.
XD-ADR-0065.title: Provenance trailer on GitHub posts

XD-ADR-0066.content: **New repo ``robarm-integration``.** It holds system test cases (``INT-STC``), integration test cases (``INT-ITC``), the HIL setups, and the **orphan evidence branch** for HIL runs. Revises :need:`XD-ADR-0050`, which put that branch in robarm-sw. robarm-syseng stays the left side of the V (needs, requirements, model).
XD-ADR-0066.title: An integration repo for system tests and HIL

XD-ADR-0067.content: **Prototype wiring is EE content** in robarm-ee: a KiCad schematic of each prototype setup, whose elements are ``EE-CMP`` with ``variant: prototype``. They realize the ``SYS-PROTO`` / ``SYS-EL`` elements. Field changed by :need:`XD-ADR-0093` (``configs``).
XD-ADR-0067.title: Prototype wiring is EE content

XD-ADR-0068.content: **Retired needs get a grace period until the next baseline.** On ``main`` and in PRs, a link to a ``retired`` need is a reported warning that doesn't fail the build. The baseline build fails while any such link remains. Refines :need:`XD-ADR-0057` (e).
XD-ADR-0068.title: A grace period for retired needs

XD-ADR-0069.content: **SW architecture** is written in rst in iteration 1. A SysML SW sub-model in robarm-sw is tried in iteration 2.
XD-ADR-0069.title: SW architecture in rst in iteration 1

XD-ADR-0070.content: **Code links:** a code unit (``SW-IMPL``) must ``implements`` a SW design element. It **may also ``satisfies`` a ``SW-REQ`` directly**, as in the safety repo.
XD-ADR-0070.title: Code units implement design elements

XD-ADR-0071.content: **ID format** ``<DOMAIN>-<KIND>-<NNNN>`` with a 4-digit number. Domains are ``SYS``, ``SW``, ``EE``, ``ME``, ``INT``. Examples: ``SYS-REQ-0012``, ``SW-TC-0103``, ``EE-CMP-0007``. Test results: ``TR-<test case ID>-<run hash>``.
XD-ADR-0071.title: ID format DOMAIN-KIND-NNNN

XD-ADR-0072.content: **No project code in the sources.** A project code with the separator ``:`` (e.g. ``RA:SYS-REQ-0012``) is added only where IDs leave the workspace: bundles, published ``needs.json``, shared affirmatrix cases.
XD-ADR-0072.title: No project code in the sources

XD-ADR-0073.content: **SW test case IDs** come from the ledger and are written into the ZTEST comment by a tool, like safety's ``@testid``.
XD-ADR-0073.title: SW test case IDs come from the ledger

XD-ADR-0074.content: The **problem statement** (SYSMOD step 03) is a ``SYS-NEED`` with ``category: problem``. Other needs and objectives link to it with ``addresses``. A ``concern`` stub is generated for it.
XD-ADR-0074.title: The problem statement is a stakeholder need

XD-ADR-0075.content: **System objectives** (SYSMOD step 06) are ``SYS-NEED`` with ``category: objective``. No separate kind.
XD-ADR-0075.title: System objectives are stakeholder needs

XD-ADR-0076.content: **Requirement values** (quantity, unit, min/max/nominal, EARS pattern) are need fields next to the EARS text. They are copied into the ``requirement`` stubs as attributes and checked against the sentence.
XD-ADR-0076.title: Requirement values are need fields

XD-ADR-0077.content: The **SYSMOD v5 library** (``mbse4u/sysmod-sysmlv2``) is a **west project** pinned at a commit. Sysand stays optional.
XD-ADR-0077.title: The SYSMOD library is a pinned west project

XD-ADR-0078.content: Iteration 1 includes a **short functional architecture** (SYSMOD 10a): functions realize use cases, and logical elements realize functions (``functional2logical``). ``SYS-EL`` gets a ``layer`` field (``functional``, ``logical``, ``product``).
XD-ADR-0078.title: A short functional architecture

XD-ADR-0079.content: **West submanifests and project groups.** The manifest repo splits its project list into submanifest files (one per area, e.g. framework, syseng, ee, me, sw, integration), imported by the main ``west.yml``. Projects carry **groups**, so each engineer or agent checks out only what their role needs (``manifest.group-filter``). A role's group set always includes its upstream repos and the framework (:need:`XD-ADR-0029`, :need:`XD-ADR-0059`). Details are in task 3.4.
XD-ADR-0079.title: West submanifests and project groups

XD-ADR-0080.content: **Component libraries are pinned west projects, isolated from user-global setups.** EE uses the tiacsys KiCad libraries (``kicad-symbols``, ``kicad-footprints``, ``kicad-packages3D``, ``kicad-templates``, ``kicad-library-utils``). ME uses the FreeCAD parts library (``FreeCAD/FreeCAD-library``). KiCad projects use project-local library tables that point into the workspace through variables, and the GUI launchers (:need:`XD-ADR-0060`, 3.13) set those variables. FreeCAD gets its parts path from its launcher. User-global libraries are not used. The big libraries (``kicad-packages3D`` about 1.8 GB, FreeCAD-library about 5.7 GB) get their own groups (:need:`XD-ADR-0079`) and shallow clones.
XD-ADR-0080.title: Pinned, isolated component libraries

XD-ADR-0081.content: **Bump bot = a scheduled poll** in robarm-manifest (e.g. every 30 min, plus manual). It uses its own ``GITHUB_TOKEN``, so no extra secret is needed. Because PRs opened with that token don't trigger CI, the job builds the full set itself and reports on the bump PR. Refines :need:`XD-ADR-0054`.
XD-ADR-0081.title: The bump bot is a scheduled poll

XD-ADR-0082.content: The **integration role** checks out everything except the big libraries (KiCad 3D models, FreeCAD parts).
XD-ADR-0082.title: The integration role

XD-ADR-0083.content: **Workspace paths:** design repos at the top level; dependencies under ``tools/`` (zdocs, affirmatrix) and ``libs/`` (SYSMOD, KiCad, FreeCAD).
XD-ADR-0083.title: Workspace paths

XD-ADR-0084.content: The manifest's **default group filter is minimal** (framework, syseng, Zephyr). Each role switches its groups on.
XD-ADR-0084.title: A minimal default group filter

XD-ADR-0085.content: **View definitions live in the model:** SysML v2 `view`s (in ``views.sysml``) with ``expose``/``filter`` and an ``@XdView`` annotation naming the view kind.
XD-ADR-0085.title: View definitions live in the model

XD-ADR-0086.content: **Trace graphs** are drawn with sphinx-needs ``needflow`` (graphviz), not drawio. The user has a separate tool for analysing trace graphs interactively in the works.
XD-ADR-0086.title: Trace graphs with needflow

XD-ADR-0087.content: **Views are committed as editable SVG** (``<view>.drawio.svg``: the rendered picture with the drawio diagram embedded). They are rendered locally with stable IDs and a hash of the embedded diagram. CI checks the content against the model and the freshness of the picture, without a browser. Refines :need:`XD-ADR-0032`.
XD-ADR-0087.title: Views are committed as editable SVG

XD-ADR-0088.content: **drawio desktop 31.7.0** is installed as a system package (``/usr/bin/drawio``). It is used to open and arrange views, and to test the editor round trip.
XD-ADR-0088.title: drawio desktop 31.7.0

XD-ADR-0089.content: **One xdmod tool, ``curatrix``,** with subcommands ``check``, ``gen``, ``ids``, ``views`` and later ``bootstrap``/``launch``. Refines :need:`XD-ADR-0042` for the framework's own tooling.
XD-ADR-0089.title: One framework tool: curatrix

XD-ADR-0090.content: **Verification coverage** (:need:`XD-CHECK-0007`, rule :need:`XD-RULE-0009`) is a warning in iteration 1, and an error at the baseline gate from iteration 2.
XD-ADR-0090.title: Verification coverage is a warning in iteration 1

XD-ADR-0091.content: **Pre-commit hooks** (normalizers, ID placeholders, fast checks) are installed by the bootstrap in every active repo.
XD-ADR-0091.title: Pre-commit hooks

XD-ADR-0092.content: **Variants follow VAMOS, in SysML v2 through PLEML** (MBSE4U, MIT, pinned west project). The core is the functional and logical architecture. A feature model, a 150 % product architecture with variation points bound to features, and one product model per configuration complete it. Revises :need:`XD-ADR-0031`.
XD-ADR-0092.title: Variants follow VAMOS through PLEML

XD-ADR-0093.content: **Variant fields:** design elements and test cases carry ``configs`` (list of ``SYS-CFG`` IDs, derived where possible), requirements carry ``where`` (feature condition, matching EARS "Where …"), and test results carry ``config``. These replace the ``variant`` field of :need:`XD-ADR-0031`; :need:`XD-ADR-0067`'s prototype wiring uses ``configs``.
XD-ADR-0093.title: Variant fields configs, where and config

XD-ADR-0094.content: **Coverage per configuration:** requirements carry ``verification_scope`` (``logical``: evidence from any configuration counts; ``config``: evidence needed per applicable configuration). The coverage report is a requirement × configuration matrix.
XD-ADR-0094.title: Coverage per configuration

XD-ADR-0095.content: **Variant rules** :need:`XD-RULE-0021` and :need:`XD-RULE-0022` (feature model), :need:`XD-RULE-0023` to :need:`XD-RULE-0028` (product models), and :need:`XD-RULE-0029` to :need:`XD-RULE-0031` (traces) are the variant part of the trace rules. XD-ADR-0126.content:
**Accepted CAD findings live in one file format for EE and ME:** ``pcba/<name>/accepted.yaml`` and
``assemblies/<name>/accepted.yaml``, read by the same check code. An entry names the check, the
rule, the items (designators or part names, never positions, so the entry survives a move; or all
findings of one rule, as for unrouted nets) and the reason.

**Only a human accepts.** An entry counts as accepted only when the commit that added it carries an
explicit ``Accepted-by: <name>`` trailer, has no agent trailer, and changes nothing but acceptance
entries. Agents never write ``Accepted-by:``; an entry from an agent commit, or not yet committed,
is a proposal (:need:`XD-ADR-0051`): a warning locally, an error at the baseline. Real enforcement
(commits signed with a key only the owner holds) stays in iteration 2 (:need:`XD-ADR-0123`).

- Only errors must be accepted; warnings are listed and never fail.
- KiCad's own exclusions stay for single, stable findings, under the same rule: an exclusion
  counts as accepted only when the commit that added it to the ``.kicad_pro`` carries
  ``Accepted-by:``, has no agent trailer and changes nothing but exclusions or acceptance entries;
  otherwise it is a proposal. Stated rule: a KiCad exclusion is lost when its items move. An ERC exclusion counts only if no finding of the same type and items is
  reported as not excluded, because KiCad turns a stale ERC exclusion into an excluded phantom
  finding (KiCad spike §4.4).
- A board's ERC and DRC severities must equal those of the ``curatrix new pcba`` template (a
  missing ``erc`` section counts as KiCad's defaults). A difference is a finding that needs
  acceptance, so a severity cannot silently switch a rule off.
- The reports stay local; CI and Pages show a placeholder in the findings section.
XD-ADR-0126.title: One accepted.yaml format, with Accepted-by

XD-ADR-0127.content:
**WireViz is adopted** for cables between boards and external parts. It is a pinned pip package
(xdmod ``requirements.txt``), plain Python with Graphviz, so CI and Pages can draw the diagrams
too. Licence check (2026-11-17): WireViz is GPL-3.0, xdmod is Apache-2.0. curatrix runs the
``wireviz`` command as a separate process through ``curatrix run`` and never imports it, so it is
used as a tool; its output (diagrams, BOMs) is not covered by the GPL. Each harness is one folder ``harness/<name>/`` with one WireViz YAML ``<name>.yml`` as entry
point, 1:1 with a cable def in the EE model (``EE-HAR``, :need:`XD-ADR-0128`). The connectors at
both ends name the ``EE-PORT`` they mate with, also on external parts; CK-F1 checks pin to pin
against both ends. ``curatrix cam`` makes the diagram, the harness BOM (with Manufacturer and MPN)
and the version from tags ``<name>/vX.Y.Z``. One harness in iteration 1. The harness length and
route are a co-design value between EE and ME (task 5.28). Prototype jumper wiring stays a KiCad
schematic per prototype setup (:need:`XD-ADR-0067`).
XD-ADR-0127.title: WireViz for harnesses

XD-ADR-0128.content:
**The domain model emits the** ``EE-PCBA``, ``EE-PORT``, ``EE-HAR``, ``ME-ASM`` **and**
``ME-PORT`` **needs.** The ID is the short name of the def in the domain model. KiCad, WireViz and
FreeCAD files carry these IDs only as references: the ``TraceID`` of a KiCad project or of the top
FreeCAD document of an assembly, the ``Port`` field of a KiCad connector, the ``Port`` property of
a FreeCAD LCS, the port names at both ends of a harness. The ``Realizes`` and ``Conforms`` fields on
KiCad projects and FreeCAD documents go away: these links are derived from specialization
(:need:`XD-ADR-0132`). ``EE-CMP`` and ``ME-PART`` stay owned by the CAD files, as before
(:need:`XD-ADR-0023`).

**One CAD file per domain def.** Each board def has exactly one KiCad project
``pcba/<name>/<name>.kicad_pro``, each cable def exactly one harness folder ``harness/<name>/``, each
assembly or sub-assembly def exactly one FreeCAD document; and each of these files names exactly
one def. The folder name comes from the element name (``JointController`` →
``joint-controller``). The project's entry point is its ``.kicad_pro``; the root schematic has the
same name. Instances are usages of the def, in any number; the trace stays on the def
(:need:`XD-ADR-0117`). A single ME part is 1:1 with a model element only when the model treats it
as a block. The CK-D4 readers change with this decision.
XD-ADR-0128.title: The domain model owns the IDs of boards, assemblies, ports and harnesses

XD-ADR-0129.content:
**Each board, harness and top-level assembly gets its own document from the start:**
``pcba-<name>`` (and ``proto-<name>`` per prototype project), ``harness-<name>`` and ``asm-<name>``
(with one chapter per sub-assembly). ``ee-design`` and ``me-design`` keep the requirements and the
overview. ``curatrix new pcba`` / ``new asm`` create the document and its registry entry. One
directive set per document type, so all documents of one type look the same; a section without
data prints one fixed sentence.

**What CI can show:** everything read in plain Python appears everywhere: stackup and design-rule
tables, connector pin tables (from the committed ``generated/<project>.connectors.json``), the
BOM (in the appendix, one column per variant), the variants table, parameters, materials and
interfaces of assemblies, the harness diagram and pin-to-pin table. What needs KiCad or FreeCAD
(schematic, renderings, ERC/DRC findings, drawings, exploded view, mass and center of gravity) is
included only in local builds, from ``build/<repo>/cam/``, with the version it shows; CI and Pages
show a placeholder. At the baseline stage, missing or stale local output is an error. A board or
harness appears in the assembly BOM as one line with its version and a link to its document.
XD-ADR-0129.title: One document per board, harness and assembly

XD-ADR-0130.content:
**The EE and ME repos each have their own SysML model in** ``model/`` **and refine the system
model by specialization.** SW keeps its architecture in rst in iteration 1 (:need:`XD-ADR-0069`);
a SW sub-model would follow the same pattern in iteration 2. There are three levels of detail:

- **System model** (the systems engineering repo): what crosses a domain boundary. Blocks down to
  the product level (one part def per board, assembly and SW component), their ports, and the
  interface defs (``SYS-IF``) at signal level: signal names, direction, kind, values from the
  requirements. No connector types, pin numbers or part numbers.
- **Domain model** (``<domain repo>/model/``): how the domain realizes a block. EE: board defs,
  connector port defs with connector type and pin map (pin number and net name per signal), cable
  defs, external parts, board variants. ME: assembly and sub-assembly defs, mechanical port defs
  with geometry, assembly variants. In iteration 1 there are no circuit block diagrams inside a
  board.
- **Implementation** (KiCad projects, WireViz files, FreeCAD documents): they name the domain
  model elements they implement.

A domain def specializes the system def it realizes (``part def JointControllerBoard :>
JointController``) and redefines every inherited port with a port whose def specializes the
interface def (``port def ServoHeader :> ServoIf``). A domain def may specialize several system
defs; a name clash between inherited ports is solved by one port that redefines all of them
(``port :>> A::p, B::p : X;``). Redefined signal ports repeat their direction (``out port :>>
pwm``). Inside a def that specializes a system def, outer elements are named by qualified name,
because inherited members hide outer names.

A domain model imports only the system model and the xdmod libraries; SW reads the EE model
(:need:`XD-ADR-0131`). It reads the upstream model twice, both from the same west pin: as a
library set for the Pilot, and as the upstream's committed ``generated/model.json`` for the
checks that run without Java. The repo's own model files are read as one set, so their order does
not matter. Each domain model costs one more Pilot run; the owner accepted that. Based on the
model spike (``claude/notes/model-spike.md``).
XD-ADR-0130.title: Domain repos refine the system model by specialization

XD-ADR-0131.content:
**First exception to the peer rule: SW is downstream of EE for the board model.** The MCU pin map
of a board is an EE design decision, so it lives in the EE model, not in a ``SYS-IF``. SW reads it
from there: SW needs (``SW-ARCH``, ``SW-DD``) may ``conforms`` to an ``EE-PCBA`` or an
``EE-PORT``, the SW repo lists the EE documents and the EE model as upstream, and the sw role gets
the EE repo. EE never links to SW. The direction stays acyclic: syseng → EE → SW. CK-F2
(devicetree against the model) compares with the EE board model. In iteration 1 the devicetree is
written by hand; a generator from KiCad is iteration 2. Each Zephyr board variant maps to one
board variant by name, and SW adds no board variants of its own in iteration 1.
XD-ADR-0131.title: SW reads the board pin maps from EE

XD-ADR-0132.content:
**Conformance is a curatrix check, not a Pilot result.** The Pilot finds neither a missing
redefinition nor a redefinition with the wrong port def. So curatrix checks, on the committed
model JSON of the domain repo and its upstream: every port that a domain def inherits from a
system def is redefined somewhere in the chain between the two, and the most specific
redefinition's def specializes the inherited port's def. The same rule holds inside port defs at
signal level. A variant def of a board does not repeat the redefinitions of its parent. An
unsolved name clash of inherited ports is an error.

**Links come from specialization.** ``curatrix gen model`` turns a ``:>`` across the repo boundary
into a trace link on the domain need, chosen by the pair of kinds: ``EE-PCBA`` / ``ME-ASM`` /
``EE-HAR`` to ``SYS-EL`` is ``realizes``; ``EE-PORT`` / ``ME-PORT`` to ``SYS-IF`` is ``conforms``.
Any other pair is a finding, never skipped. A def without an ID of its own that specializes a
system element is allowed only below the port level (for example a signal def inside a port def);
anywhere else it is a warning.
XD-ADR-0132.title: curatrix checks conformance and derives the links

XD-ADR-0133.content:
**Three new need kinds.**

- ``EE-PORT``: a connector port of a board, or a port of an external part, in the EE model. It
  ``conforms`` to the ``SYS-IF`` it specializes and is ``part_of`` its board (``EE-PCBA``). A port
  of an external part has no ``part_of``; its qualified name names the part. A KiCad connector
  names it in its ``Port`` field; a connector without a port says so with ``Port = -``.
- ``ME-PORT``: a mechanical interface of an assembly in the ME model, with its geometry. It
  ``conforms`` to the ``SYS-IF`` it specializes and is ``part_of`` its assembly (``ME-ASM``). In
  FreeCAD it is an LCS with a ``Port`` property.
- ``EE-HAR``: a wiring harness, 1:1 with a cable def in the EE model. It ``connects`` the two or more
  ``EE-PORT`` s its ends mate with. The harness is built to fit those ports, so it is the more
  concrete side and holds the link (:need:`XD-ADR-0004`). Like every design element it must
  ``realizes`` a ``SYS-EL`` or ``satisfies`` an ``EE-REQ`` (no orphans, :need:`XD-RULE-0010`); it may
  also ``conforms`` to a ``SYS-IF``. Ports are not in the orphan rule: a port of an external part
  may conform to nothing.
XD-ADR-0133.title: Need kinds EE-PORT, ME-PORT and EE-HAR

XD-ADR-0134.content:
**Second exception to the peer rule: ME may write into EE's KiCad project, but only inside a
co-design change.** The space a board may take is a ``SYS-IF`` budget in the system model: a port
def with a box (``width``, ``depth``, ``heightAbove``, ``heightBelow``), a hole list
(``hole<n>X``, ``hole<n>Y``, ``holeDiameter``) and connector positions (``<ref>X``, ``<ref>Y``,
pin 1), in the board frame (origin at the lower-left corner of the outline seen from the top, x
right, y up, z = 0 on the top face). The values are defaults, so a domain def can restate them.
The board def conforms to it by ``dependency from <board> to <budget>`` (a budget is no connector
port); the ME port def of the board seat specializes it and restates the values FreeCAD needs.
**Open for the owner:** the restated budget values (the attributes that redefine an attribute of
the ``SYS-IF`` budget, not the placement and not attributes ME adds itself) are copied from the
system model, not chosen in ME, so this decision proposes that they do not count toward the "at
most ten driving parameters" of :need:`XD-ADR-0137`. That is an interpretation of XD-ADR-0137,
although the copies drive the sketch ``BoardOutline``; the owner decides it when accepting this
decision. A geometry change is one change with one branch name over the systems engineering, ME
and EE repos (:need:`XD-ADR-0045`).

**The push is one tool step on copies:** the sketch ``BoardOutline`` of the skeleton (driven by
the parameters) goes into a copy of the ``.kicad_pcb`` by KiCad StepUp (``export_pcb``), run from
a script in the FreeCAD GUI binary offscreen, with ``HOME`` set to a folder under ``.xdmod/`` for
that process only (StepUp writes ``~/ksu-config.ini``); then ``kicad-cli pcb upgrade --force``
re-saves the copy in the KiCad 10 format, DRC runs on it, and only then the file goes back into
the EE repo. StepUp is pinned by commit under ``.xdmod/stepup/`` (pin and licence gap:
:ref:`howto-co-design-change`). It pushes the outline and the holes
(as ``Edge.Cuts`` circles, non-plated cut-outs); the board frame lands on the grid origin, or on
the lower-left corner of the old outline. The EE side reviews and merges its part. ME never takes
EE geometry outside such a change, and ME needs never link to EE needs.

**Scope in iteration 1** (co-design spike, ``claude/notes/codesign-spike.md``): keep-out zones
are not pushed (the box covers the space; StepUp could push them, iteration 2). Connector
positions are budget values, but never pushed: EE places connectors, and a planned check (task
5.25) compares them. EE does not push back through StepUp: the board model reaches FreeCAD by the
scripted STEP path (``kicad-cli pcb export step``, headless import), because StepUp's board load
stalls offscreen; a change EE needs (a bigger box, a moved hole) is a budget change in the same
co-design branch. A harness length is a ``SYS-IF`` value its cable def conforms to like a board
(``EE-HAR`` to ``SYS-IF``); its route in the ME assembly is iteration 2.
XD-ADR-0134.title: ME writes board geometry into KiCad in a co-design change

XD-ADR-0135.content:
**Bought boards and parts are external parts:** a def in the EE model with their headers or
terminals as ports (``EE-PORT``), but no KiCad project. They are outside the 1:1 project rule
(:need:`XD-ADR-0128`). Examples: an MCU evaluation board, a PWM or ADC breakout, a servo, a
potentiometer. Harness ends and prototype wiring name their ports, and CK-F1 checks against them.

**A prototype project** ``proto/<name>/<name>.kicad_pro`` **is 1:1 with a block of the prototype
configuration** in the system model (for example ``JointProtoRig``), like a board project with its
board def. Its schematic shows the wiring between external parts (:need:`XD-ADR-0067`).
XD-ADR-0135.title: External parts and prototype projects

XD-ADR-0136.content:
**Board and assembly variants are named in the domain model.** Each domain variant names the
system configurations (``SYS-CFG``) and usages it serves (``Configs``). The table
"configuration → variant per usage" is computed, like a backlink; nobody writes it. A check in the
domain repo, against the published needs of the systems engineering repo: exactly one variant per
usage and configuration, and the variant exists in the domain model and in KiCad or FreeCAD. At
most two variants per board and per assembly in iteration 1. Unused variants are not reported in
iteration 1.

**EE:** board variants are KiCad assembly variants. A solder jumper or 0 Ω link is fitted (=
bridged) or DNP per variant. The position of a pin-header shunt is set by hand after assembly, so
it is not an assembly matter: the EE model holds it per variant (with its meaning, for example an
I²C address), and the KiCad part carries the same value in a per-variant field ``Setting`` (KiCad
10 can override any field per variant, KiCad spike §3.3), so the BOM shows it. A check compares
the variant names and settings in the EE model, the ``.kicad_pro``, the ``.kicad_sch`` and the
``.kicad_pcb``. Each Zephyr board variant maps to one board variant by name (checked on the
canary). ME variants: :need:`XD-ADR-0137`.
XD-ADR-0136.title: Variants: the domain variant names what it serves

XD-ADR-0137.content:
**Each top-level assembly is a folder** ``assemblies/<name>/`` with its top document
``<name>.FCStd``, a skeleton document ``skeleton.FCStd``, and its own parts; shared parts stay in
``parts/``. The skeleton holds the parameter spreadsheet ``Params`` and the master sketch. The
master sketch cannot live in the top document: parts that refer to it would form a document cycle,
and FreeCAD then recomputes in an undefined order (FreeCAD spike §1). Parts refer only to the
skeleton, never to the top document; the top document links the skeleton and the parts. At most ten
driving parameters in iteration 1.

**The model drives the CAD.** ``curatrix gen freecad-params`` writes the model values into
``Params`` (aliases ``<port>_<attribute>``): it opens the top document first, writes values only
(it never rebuilds objects, so object IDs do not churn), recomputes skeleton, parts, sub-assemblies
and top in this order, and saves only the documents whose values changed. CK-F3 checks that they
agree.

**Interfaces** are LCS with a ``Port`` property (the ``ME-PORT`` ID). **Variants** are rows of a
configuration table in ``Params`` plus ``Configs`` on the links; part presence comes from
``Configs``, never from a suppressed state. Checks, value writes and the exploded view run in
``FreeCADCmd``. The exploded view uses the fallback of the FreeCAD spike (§5): the moves are data
(a small table per assembly, or read from the ``Move`` objects in ``Document.xml``), and a script
builds the exploded compound and its TechDraw view; the Assembly workbench's exploded view in the

XD-ADR-0138.content:
**The systems engineering repo owns the usages it sees** (the blocks of the product architecture,
for example six joints). A domain model refers to them and does not repeat them. **The domain model
owns its internal usages** (sub-assemblies and parts that the system model never sees). The check
that counts FreeCAD links per part or sub-assembly against the usages uses both, filtered by
``Configs`` per variant. Instances may differ only through variants (:need:`XD-ADR-0136`); in
iteration 1 they get no IDs of their own.
XD-ADR-0138.title: Who owns instance counts

XD-ADR-0139.content:
**FreeCAD models of the boards live in their own repo,** ``robarm-freecad-pcba`` in the robot arm
(path ``libs/freecad-pcba``, in a west group that the ee and me roles both get). EE writes into it,
ME reads from it, so neither depends on the other's repo. Only tagged board versions go in
(:need:`XD-ADR-0140`): ``kicad-cli pcb export step`` with the variant and the version, then a
headless FreeCAD import that adds the board's ``EE-PCBA`` ID and version as properties. The EE agent
opens the PR that adds a board version. At most 5 MB per file to start (board body, connectors and
tall parts, no tracks). An ME assembly links one fixed board version; a newer version gives a note
or an issue on the ME repo, and moving to it is an ME change. Creating the repo is an admin action
that needs the owner's approval (:need:`XD-ADR-0112`). Proposed until task 5.29 has shown the
headless STEP import (the FreeCAD spike did not test it).
XD-ADR-0139.title: A board library repo for ME

XD-ADR-0140.content:
**Boards, assemblies and harnesses have their own tags** ``<name>/vX.Y.Z`` (for example
``joint-controller/v1.2.0``) in their domain repo, next to the repo tags (:need:`XD-ADR-0047`). The
design output takes its version from ``git describe --match '<name>/*'``. ME tags only assemblies;
an exported part carries the version of the assembly. **Only the owner creates these tags**, like
baselines; an agent proposes a tag in its PR. Unfinished designs use ``v0.x`` tags, as the owner set for the canary (Phase 5 plan review, P5-12).

XD-ADR-0141.content:

- **me** also needs the EE repo with the KiCad libraries (west group ``ee``, without the 3D models)

``tools.yaml`` and the roles of ``curatrix bootstrap`` follow; ``curatrix doctor`` warns when a role
with ``kicad-cli`` has no KiCad 3D models (STEP and renderings then show bare boards).
XD-ADR-0141.title: Roles: EE gets FreeCAD, ME gets the KiCad files, SW gets the EE model

XD-ADR-0142.content:
**The EE part of the CAM pipeline moves into iteration 1.** ``curatrix cam <repo> [<project>]``
copies the KiCad project into ``build/<repo>/cam/<project>/<version>/``, writes the version into
the copy's ``.kicad_pro`` text variable ``XD_VERSION`` and runs the jobset there with ``kicad-cli
jobset run``. The committed project keeps ``XD_VERSION = "unversioned"``.

- **Version:** ``git describe --match '<project>/*'`` (:need:`XD-ADR-0140`). A dirty tree, or a
  commit that is not on ``main`` or a baseline, gives a version marked as preview; without a tag
  it is ``<project>/v0.0.0-<n>-g<sha>-preview``. The full version goes into a title-block comment
  line and a silkscreen text; the ``Rev`` field cuts long strings off, so it holds only the short
  version or nothing.
- **Jobset:** one shared template in xdmod, copied by ``curatrix new pcba``. A job can name a
  variant (KiCad 10.0.8, KiCad spike §2.2), so the jobset holds one job per variant-dependent output
  and variant, copied from its base job except for the variant and file name; the variant names in
  the jobs equal those of the project. No "Execute Command" jobs, no "Copy Files" outside the
  output folder, no statistics job, BOM delimiters set, ERC and DRC not in the jobset (the checks
  evaluate them). curatrix fails the run when fewer jobs ran than the jobset has (a job KiCad
  cannot parse drops all jobs with exit code 0).
- **Outputs:** Gerber and drill, pick-and-place, netlist, STEP, top and bottom renderings
  (orthographic) and one 3D rendering, schematic PDF and SVG, BOM CSV. The stackup table (and an
  optional SVG cross-section) and the design-rule table come from plain Python, because KiCad
  exports neither.
- **Where:** output only under ``build/``, never committed, no release asset, run only locally (no
  KiCad in CI). The bundle stays in iteration 2. KiCad batch runs use the workspace-local
  configuration, cache and documents folders, the C locale and a ``TMPDIR`` under ``build/``, one
  after the other.
XD-ADR-0142.title: EE design output in iteration 1

XD-ADR-0143.content:
**The ME part of the CAM pipeline moves into iteration 1.** ``curatrix cam <repo> <asm>`` runs
FreeCAD headless under limits into ``build/<repo>/cam/<asm>/<version>/``: STEP of the assembly; 3MF
and STL per printed part with its print profile (:need:`XD-ADR-0024`); TechDraw drawings as PDF and
SVG; the exploded view as a TechDraw view SVG, built in ``FreeCADCmd`` (:need:`XD-ADR-0137`); a flat BOM
CSV with totals. Per variant: set the variant row, recompute, export, close without saving;
presence by ``Configs``. The version comes from the assembly tags (:need:`XD-ADR-0140`), with the
same preview marking as EE. A shared part from ``parts/`` carries the version of the assembly
being exported.

**Version on printed parts:** a part marks the face for it with an LCS (``Role =
version-emboss``, text size, maximum width). At export, and only there, curatrix embosses the
short version (the full string goes into the drawing) with a font pinned in xdmod; the
``.FCStd`` stays unchanged, and the export fails unless the result is exactly one valid solid.
GLB is deferred; renderings come at the end of Phase 5 (task 5.30). Output only under ``build/``,
only locally. Based on the FreeCAD spike (§5, §6).
XD-ADR-0143.title: ME design output in iteration 1

XD-ADR-0145.content:
**Never run KiCad or FreeCAD outside curatrix or its shims, not even** ``--version``. A bare
``kicad-cli --version`` rewrites ``~/.config/kicad/10.0/kicad_common.json``; agents did this twice.
As a safety net, ``curatrix bootstrap`` and ``update`` write shims into the main workspace's
``.venv/bin`` (also when run from a worktree set) for every KiCad and FreeCAD program on the machine:
``kicad-cli``, ``kicad``, ``eeschema``, ``pcbnew``, ``bitmap2component``, each program with a KiCad
``.kiface`` (``gerbview``, ``pl_editor``, ``pcb_calculator``, ...) and every ``freecad*`` program in any
case (``FreeCAD``, ``FreeCADCmd``, ``freecad``, ``freecadcmd``, ...). A shim sets the workspace-local
config that ``curatrix run`` sets (``LC_ALL`` only for ``kicad-cli``; the GUIs keep the user's
locale) and runs the real binary, found by absolute path when the shim is written (never
``.venv/bin`` itself or another shim). KiCad's IDF converters (``idfcyl``, ``dxf2idf``, ...) write no
config and get no shim. ``curatrix env`` puts ``.venv/bin`` first on ``PATH``; ``curatrix doctor`` warns when
a KiCad or FreeCAD name on ``PATH`` is not the shim, or a shim's real binary is gone. Nothing outside the workspace changes: no
user-global files, no ``PATH`` edits in shell profiles. The shims set no limits, so the tools still
run through curatrix (:need:`XD-ADR-0064`).
XD-ADR-0145.title: KiCad and FreeCAD never run outside curatrix; shims in .venv/bin

XD-ADR-0146.content:
Proposed by the agent of tasks 5.23 and 5.24, for the owner to accept or change; it states what
the code of these tasks does where it differs from :need:`XD-ADR-0137`.

- **The skeleton is** ``assemblies/<name>/<name>-skeleton.FCStd``, not ``skeleton.FCStd``.
  FreeCAD names a document after its file, and a cross-document expression names that document
  (``canary_assembly_skeleton#MasterSketch.Constraints.partLength``). With one file name for every
  skeleton, two assemblies opened together clash, and a later rename touches every part
  expression.
- **The parameter aliases are** ``<usage>_<attribute>``: the usage is a port or a part usage of the
  top-level assembly def (``mount_x``, ``canaryPart_length``), so a main dimension of a part can be
  a parameter too; :need:`XD-ADR-0137` said ``<port>_<attribute>``.
- **The writer opens the skeleton first, then the top document.** The top document links only the
  part ``Skeleton`` of the skeleton, so through the top FreeCAD loads the skeleton only partially,
  without ``Params`` (found in task 5.24). The skeleton depends on no other document; the parts
  then load fully through the top. The writer stops when any document is still partial.
- Parts that take values from a skeleton belong to that assembly and sit in its folder
  (``assemblies/<name>/parts/``); a shared part in ``parts/`` takes no value from a skeleton.
XD-ADR-0146.title: FreeCAD assemblies: skeleton file name, parameter aliases, open order
